title: tests/common: MemoryBackend in-memory MailBackend impl
description:
Create tests/common/mod.rs with a complete in-memory MailBackend implementation. This is both the integration test harness and the canonical example for implementors.

## What to implement

MemoryBackend struct with:
- mailboxes: HashMap<AccountId, HashMap<Id, Mailbox>>
- emails: HashMap<AccountId, HashMap<Id, Email>>
- threads: HashMap<AccountId, HashMap<Id, Thread>>
- identities: HashMap<AccountId, HashMap<Id, Identity>>
- submissions: HashMap<AccountId, HashMap<Id, EmailSubmission>>
- vacation_response: HashMap<AccountId, Option<VacationResponse>>
- state counters: HashMap<AccountId, u64>

Implement MailBackend for MemoryBackend:
- All CRUD methods: in-memory HashMap operations
- changes_objects: linear scan of state counters
- query_objects: sort/filter in memory
- import_email: parse blob bytes, store as Email
- parse_email: parse bytes, return Email without storing
- copy_email: deep-copy email across accounts
- search_snippets: substring search in email body/subject

Helper: fn next_state(account_id) -> State — increment counter, return as State string

## Source references
- Copy pattern: ~/PROJECT/crate-jmapchat-server/jmapchat-server/tests/common/mod.rs (RefStore)
- Stalwart integration tests for expected behavior: ~/GIT/stalwart-jmap-server/main/tests/src/jmap/
- MemoryBackend does NOT need to be efficient — correct is sufficient

## Acceptance criteria
- cargo test -p jmap-mail-server --test integration passes (once tests exist)
- MemoryBackend::default() gives a working backend
- All MailBackend methods implemented (no todo! macros)
- Used in every integration test in tests/
